doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

title: Retirement, Covid and My Fair Lady
summary: He keeps busy outdoors, returns to clarinet for a Broadway show of My Fair Lady and helps a friend with a soprano sax piece.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So you wrote that you’re kinda, sorta, retired.
How do you fill your time these days?
Oh what I do is, if it’s in the summer I’m working outside a whole lot. I’ve got a chain saw and that kind of thing. But I still, with Covid I thought okay this kind of has stopped

everything. Because the gigs just stopped. And so I looked and Jeez it was a year and a half and I hadn’t practiced anything. But then a couple of — one Broadway show is coming that I’m going to play. And it’s just clarinet, and I thought okay that’ll be good, I’ll do this. It’s “My Fair Lady.” It’s an old time thing, I mean old type of scoring, you know that has four woodwinds which you hardly — you never have anymore. You usually have one guy playing everything. So anyway I’m working on clarinet, you know, getting my chops back up and I’m helping a friend of mine, I’m playing through his — he’s writing a soprano saxophone piece. And I’m playing through that and helping him out on it and you know doing those kinds of things. And then just general being retired. It’s kind of nice.
